sn56.39:1.1: “Bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins who do not understand as it really is ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.39:1.2: they look up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:
sn56.39:1.3: ‘This worthy is surely one who really knows, who really sees.’
sn56.39:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, a tuft of cotton wool or kapok, light, wafted by the wind, had settled on an even piece of ground.
sn56.39:2.2: An easterly wind would drive it westward; a westerly wind would drive it eastward; a northerly wind would drive it southward; a southerly wind would drive it northward.
sn56.39:2.4: Because of the lightness of the tuft.
sn56.39:2.5: “So too, bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins who do not understand as it really is ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.39:2.6: they look up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:
sn56.39:2.7: ‘This worthy is surely one who really knows, who really sees.’
sn56.39:2.9: Because they have not seen the Four Noble Truths.
sn56.39:3.1: “But, bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins who understand as it really is ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.39:3.2: they do not look up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:
sn56.39:3.3: ‘This worthy is surely one who really knows, who really sees.’
sn56.39:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was an iron pillar or an Indra’s pillar with a deep base, securely planted, immobile, unshaking.
sn56.39:4.2: Even if a forceful blast of wind comes—whether from the east, the west, the north, or the south—that pillar would not shake, quake, or tremble.
sn56.39:4.4: Because the pillar has a deep base and is securely planted.
sn56.39:4.5: “So too, bhikkhus, those ascetics or brahmins who understand as it really is ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.39:4.6: they do not look up at the face of another ascetic or brahmin, thinking:
sn56.39:4.7: ‘This worthy is surely one who really knows, who really sees.’
sn56.39:4.9: Because, bhikkhus, they have clearly seen the Four Noble Truths.
sn56.39:4.11: The noble truth of suffering … the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
sn56.39:5.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
